exercises.prompt: Listen. When do you say this?
options: When you arrive in the evening

explanation.en: 'Good evening' is a greeting when you arrive. 'Good night' is for leaving or going to bed.
explanation.es: «Good evening» es un saludo al llegar. «Good night» es para despedirse o ir a dormir.

steps.title: My name is… / I'm… and the English alphabet

explanation.en: To introduce yourself, say 'My name is …' or 'I'm …' ('I'm' is the short form of 'I am'). To check spelling, ask 'How do you spell that?' or 'Can you spell that, please?'. English letter names are different from Spanish ones. The most confusing for Spanish speakers are the vowels A /eɪ/, E /iː/ and I /aɪ/, and G /dʒiː/, J /dʒeɪ/, H /eɪtʃ/, R /ɑːr/, W /ˈdʌbəljuː/, Y /waɪ/, Z /ziː/ (US) or /zɛd/ (UK).
explanation.es: Para presentarte di «My name is …» o «I'm …» («I'm» es la forma corta de «I am»). Para confirmar la ortografía pregunta «How do you spell that?» o «Can you spell that, please?». Los nombres de las letras son distintos en inglés. Las más confusas para hispanohablantes son las vocales A /eɪ/, E /iː/ e I /aɪ/, y G /dʒiː/, J /dʒeɪ/, H /eɪtʃ/, R /ɑːr/, W /ˈdʌbəljuː/, Y /waɪ/, Z /ziː/ (EE. UU.) o /zɛd/ (Reino Unido).

examples.en: It's D, A, N, I, E, L.
examples.es: Es D, A, N, I, E, L.

watchOut.en: E is /iː/ and I is /aɪ/ — almost the opposite of what Spanish speakers expect. Tip: 'E for email, I for Ireland'.
watchOut.es: La E suena /iː/ y la I suena /aɪ/: casi lo contrario de lo que esperamos. Truco: «E for email, I for Ireland».

steps.title: The /h/ sound: hello, hi, how
steps.focus: /h/ in hello, hi, how — a soft breath, never silent

tip.en: English /h/ is just air from your throat, softer than Spanish 'j' in 'jamón'. It is not silent at the start of hello, hi, how or he. Imagine fogging a mirror: 'ha'.
tip.es: La /h/ inglesa es solo aire de la garganta, más suave que la «j» de «jamón». No es muda al inicio de hello, hi, how o he. Imagina que empañas un espejo: «ja» muy suave.

steps.title: An email from your teacher
steps.text:
Subject: Welcome to Class 1B!

Good morning, everyone!

My name is Helen Brown. That's H, E, L, E, N — Helen. I'm your teacher.

Our class is in room fourteen. Please write your name on the paper on the door.

Questions? Ask me: 'Can you spell that, please?' or 'Sorry, can you say that again?'

See you on Monday!
Helen

exercises.prompt: What does Helen want students to do?
options: Write their name on the paper on the door
Spell their name in the email
